Report_ID: All-cause mortality at 90 days (derived from 'Survival at 90 days [Alive]')
Title: A feasibility randomised controlled trial of targeted oxygen therapy in mechanically ventilated critically ill patients (TOXYC)
Author: Martin DS, McNeil M, Brew-Graves C, Filipe H, O'Driscoll R, Stevens JL, Burnish R, Cumpstey AF, Williams NR, Mythen MG, Grocott MPW
Comment: Death counts are not stated directly; derived by subtraction from the reported numbers alive at 90 days in Table 6 (conservative: 16 with data − 9 alive = 7 deaths; control: 16 with data − 11 alive = 5 deaths). Per the synthesis plan the ITT denominator of 17 randomised per arm is used, although outcome data were missing for one participant in each arm (survival percentages in Table 6 are based on 16 per arm). No statistical test, effect size, or p-value was reported by the authors for this outcome (trial was a feasibility study, not powered).
Participant type: Mechanically ventilated critically ill adults (≥18 years) within 24 hours of unplanned ICU admission with respiratory failure
Recruitment source: Two NHS ICUs (Royal Free Hospital, London; Southampton General Hospital), February 2018 – October 2019
Outcome measurement: Number of participants dead at 90 days, derived as randomised N minus number alive reported in Table 6
Outcome variable: All-cause mortality at 90 days (derived from 'Survival at 90 days [Alive]')
effect_direction: RR ≈ 0.71 (5/17 higher vs 7/17 lower) — fewer deaths with the higher/liberal oxygen target

Title: Low versus high pulse oxygen saturation directed oxygen therapy in critically ill patients: a randomized controlled pilot study
Author: Yang, Shang, Yuan
Comment: Paper reports only counts/percentages and a chi-square P value; no risk ratio or chi-square test statistic reported. Group 1 is the higher-oxygen (intervention per synthesis plan) arm, listed second in the paper's own table.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('High SpO2 group (target SpO2 96–100%, FiO2 no lower than 30%) — higher/liberal oxygen target') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Adults (≥18 years) admitted to a general ICU with expected length of stay ≥72 hours
Recruitment source: Single-center ICU, Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Wuhan, China (Feb 17–Oct 24, 2017)
Outcome measurement: Count (percentage) of patients who died within 28 days after inclusion, intention-to-treat
effect_direction: RR ≈ 1.25 (37/114 high SpO2 vs 26/100 low SpO2) — more deaths with the higher oxygen target

Report_ID: Death from any cause at day 180
Title: Conservative Oxygen Therapy during Mechanical Ventilation in the ICU (ICU-ROX)
Author: The ICU-ROX Investigators and the ANZICS Clinical Trials Group (Mackle D, et al.)
Comment: Odds ratio and hazard ratio are reported for conservative (lower) vs usual (higher) oxygen, i.e. the inverse of the plan's higher-vs-lower direction. Event denominators reported (476 and 475) are smaller than the numbers randomised (484 conservative, 481 usual) because of missing 180-day data; randomised Ns recorded in group_1_n/group_2_n. No separate risk ratio reported for this outcome.
Participant type: Adults (≥18 years) expected to require mechanical ventilation in the ICU beyond the day after recruitment
Recruitment source: 21 intensive care units in Australia and New Zealand, September 2015 through May 2018
Outcome measurement: Number of patients who died from any cause by day 180 / number with 180-day data
Outcome variable: Death from any cause at day 180
effect_direction: RR ≈ 0.97 (164/475 usual/higher oxygen vs 170/476 conservative) — essentially no difference, marginally fewer deaths with higher target

Title: Liberal or Conservative Oxygen Therapy for Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (LOCO2)
Author: Barrot et al.
Comment: Paper's own table lists the conservative (lower-target, control per plan) arm first; group_1_is_control=True marks arm identity. Reported "difference, 14.0 percentage points (95% CI 0.7 to 27.2)" is a risk difference (conservative minus liberal), not a ratio, so it was not placed in the risk_ratio field. An adjusted hazard ratio of 1.62 (95% CI 1.02-2.56) for the conservative vs liberal survival curves is reported but is adjusted for age, Pao2:Fio2 and SAPS III and is directional for conservative, so not recorded as the unadjusted effect. Trial stopped early (205 of planned 850 enrolled).
domain: critical care medicine / oxygen therapy in ARDS
Participant type: adults with ARDS intubated and mechanically ventilated for <12 hours in the ICU
Recruitment source: 13 ICUs in France, June 2016 to September 2018
Outcome measurement: Number of patients who died from any cause by day 90 / number in the intention-to-treat population
effect_direction: RR ≈ 0.68 (31/102 liberal vs 44/99 conservative) — fewer deaths with the higher/liberal oxygen target

Report_ID: All-cause mortality within 90 days after randomization
Title: Lower or Higher Oxygenation Targets for Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure (HOT-ICU)
Author: Schjørring et al. (HOT-ICU Investigators)
Comment: The paper's own adjusted risk ratio of 1.02 (95% CI 0.94-1.11) is oriented as LOWER-oxygenation vs HIGHER-oxygenation (i.e. the inverse of the plan's higher-vs-lower orientation), so it was not entered into the risk_ratio field; raw event counts are recorded instead with group_1 = higher-oxygenation (treatment per plan). Denominators are the ITT analysed populations (1447 higher, 1441 lower) because the paper reports deaths only for these; the numbers randomised were 1466 (higher) and 1462 (lower), with 40 patients excluded for withdrawn/unobtainable consent and 1 lost to follow-up per group.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Higher-oxygenation group (PaO2 target 90 mm Hg)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Country: Denmark, Switzerland, Finland, Netherlands, Norway, United Kingdom, Iceland
Participant type: adult ICU patients (≥18 yr) with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure
Recruitment source: 35 intensive care units in 7 European countries, June 20, 2017 to August 3, 2020
Outcome measurement: Number of patients who died from any cause by day 90 / total number analysed (intention-to-treat population)
Outcome variable: All-cause mortality within 90 days after randomization
effect_direction: RR ≈ 0.99 (613/1447 higher PaO2 target vs 618/1441 lower) — no meaningful difference

Report_ID: Death from any cause at 90 days
Title: Oxygen Targets in Comatose Survivors of Cardiac Arrest (BOX trial)
Author: Schmidt et al.
Comment: Hazard ratio 0.93 (95% CI 0.72–1.20) is reported in Table 2 for restrictive vs liberal (group_1 vs group_2), i.e. the reciprocal direction to the synthesis plan's RR>1=harm-with-liberal convention; it is recorded as reported. Raw ITT event counts are supplied for RR computation. 2x2 factorial trial (oxygen × blood pressure): counts are collapsed across the blood-pressure factor, as required.
Participant type: Comatose adult survivors of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, mechanically ventilated in the ICU
Recruitment source: Two tertiary cardiac arrest centers in Denmark (Odense University Hospital; Copenhagen University Hospital Rigshospitalet), March 2017–December 2021
Outcome measurement: Number of patients who died from any cause within 90 days after randomization, out of all randomised patients (intention-to-treat)
Outcome variable: Death from any cause at 90 days
effect_direction: RR ≈ 1.08 (123/395 liberal vs 113/394 restrictive) — slightly more deaths with the higher/liberal oxygen target

Title: Conservative versus liberal oxygenation targets for mechanically ventilated patients – a pilot multicenter randomized controlled trial
Author: Panwar et al.
Comment: Conservative arm listed first in paper's table (group_1 = control/lower-oxygen arm); 104 randomised but 1 conservative-arm patient withdrew consent, so denominators are the 103 analysed (52 vs 51). Adjusted Cox HR for death by day 90 in conservative arm 0.77 (95% CI 0.40-1.50, p=0.44) reported separately but is an adjusted hazard ratio, not recorded as the pooled measure.
Participant type: Adult ICU patients (≥18 y) receiving invasive mechanical ventilation <24 h expected to continue ≥24 h
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of randomised patients dead at day 90
effect_direction: RR ≈ 0.92 (19/51 liberal vs 21/52 conservative) — slightly fewer deaths with the higher/liberal oxygen target

Report_ID: All-cause mortality 30 days after cardiac arrest
Title: Targeting two different levels of both arterial carbon dioxide and arterial oxygen after cardiac arrest and resuscitation: a randomised pilot trial (COMACARE)
Author: Jakkula et al.
Comment: Factorial trial: oxygen comparison collapsed across the co-randomised PaCO2 and MAP factors, per the synthesis plan. 123 patients were randomised but 120 were included in analyses; Table 2 denominators (61 normoxia, 59 hyperoxia) are the analysed Ns and are the only per-arm oxygen denominators reported. No effect measure (RR/OR) was reported by the paper; only counts, percentages and a p value.
Design Type: randomised controlled trial (2^3 factorial, multicentre pilot)
Participant type: Comatose, mechanically ventilated adults resuscitated from witnessed out-of-hospital cardiac arrest of presumed cardiac origin (VF/VT initial rhythm)
Recruitment source: Seven ICUs in Finland and Denmark (COMACARE study group), March 2016 - November 2017
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of patients dead at 30 days after cardiac arrest, by assigned oxygen target (collapsed across the co-randomised PaCO2 and MAP factors)
Outcome variable: All-cause mortality 30 days after cardiac arrest
effect_direction: RR ≈ 1.15 (20/59 moderate hyperoxia vs 18/61 normoxia) — more deaths with the higher oxygen target

Title: Hyperoxia and hypertonic saline in patients with septic shock (HYPERS2S): a two-by-two factorial, multicentre, randomised, clinical trial
Author: Asfar P, et al.
Comment: Denominators are the analysed ITT population reported by the paper (217 per oxygen arm); 442 were randomised (219 hyperoxia, 223 normoxia) and 8 were excluded for lack of consent for data use — randomised-arm death counts are not reported. p=0.16 is from a Cox regression; no HR for day 90 is reported numerically (HR 1.27, 0.94–1.72 is for day 28).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Hyperoxia (FiO2 1.0 for first 24 h) — higher/liberal oxygen target') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: adults (≥18 years) with fluid-refractory septic shock on mechanical ventilation in ICU
Recruitment source: 22 hospitals and academic centres in France
Outcome measurement: Number of patients who died from any cause by day 90 out of patients in the intention-to-treat population of each oxygen arm
effect_direction: RR ≈ 1.16 (104/217 hyperoxia vs 90/217 normoxia) — more deaths with the higher/liberal oxygen target
